key_reasoning.reason: One 2,884-line, 45-route router module becomes an index/ package of 10 route modules (queries, code_repositories, kb_atlassian, kb_azure_devops, kb_google, kb_sharepoint, kb_xwiki, kb_git_faq, kb_files, providers) plus two shared support modules (_common, _repository_support) and a combined-router __init__. Shared helpers are consumed across modules, but the work stays inside one subsystem and is move-only, so L rather than XL. Nearest bundled anchor is the M example epmcdme-10203 (total 15, three layers, 6 files); this change has fewer layers but a much larger module count, which is why scope scores higher and layers lower than that example. Step 2 of the same ticket scored actual M 18 for a comparable change.

diffstat reports 20 files, which maps to XXL (16+). The breakdown is 13 new package files, 1 deleted module (routers/index.py), 5 retargeted test files (191 patch strings and imports) and 1 guide row. The count is inflated by the mechanical split; per-file content is moved, not rewritten. Even so, file count alone puts the total in the M band, matching Step 2 where a 34-file change also scored M.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope held at L: refactor of a large (2,884-line, 45-route) router subsystem into a package

Technical Risk bumped from S to M: the router-level Depends(authenticate) and route-level access dependencies have to survive the move to the combined-router __init__. Sub-routers carry no auth of their own, so this is security-relevant even though no authorization behaviour changes. Existing patterns from steps 1-2 of EPMCDME-15651 cover the shape, and the OpenAPI and route_precedence baselines guard against drift, so no further bump.
